evidence: ResourceKind contains file, environment, process, port, cache, telemetry, and install labels but no CPU, memory, wall-time, or outbound-network confinement contract.
IsolationLease creates per-resource directories and holds one loopback listener; these prevent some collisions but do not constrain child resource use.
The child process receives a clean environment, private working directory, process group, wall-clock poll, and output budget, but no CPU or address-space limit and no outbound-network denial backend.
decisive_finding.impact: A fixture can exhaust host CPU or memory until the polling timeout and can make arbitrary network connections, so cross-test process/network isolation is not enforced.

contract_basis.implementation_contract: Each fixture declares isolation needs and cleanup.
contract_basis.proof_requirement: Cross-test environment, process, port, cache, telemetry, install leakage and cleanup failure must be falsified.

required_correction: Represent CPU, memory, wall-time, and outbound-network isolation needs explicitly in the fixture specification or an equally typed fail-closed policy.
Apply OS-enforced CPU and address-space limits before exec and retain the existing wall-clock kill/reap boundary.
On the supported macOS host, deny outbound network through a verified fail-closed sandbox backend; do not substitute environment labels for enforcement.
Fail closed when a requested confinement backend is unavailable or cannot be applied.
Add positive and false-pass subprocess probes for applied limits, outbound-network denial, timeout/reap, collision, cleanup, and supplied-outcome rejection.
preserved_evidence: Exact 15-file candidate identity and private root wiring were independently reproduced.
The implementation contains a real process execution path and the public caller-supplied outcome path is rejected.
claim_ceiling: No fixture scheduler source acceptance, public HCT-FIXTURES integration, routine or strict proof, readiness, release, node closure, or completion.
no_claim_statement: This decision does not claim fixture behavior, public integration, readiness, release, node closure, or goal completion.
